Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-18
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Avery Cole (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Novapay Eng Mgr), Lucas Chen (Novapay SRE), Priya Rao (Novapay CTO)

Summary:
Quick sync on throughput numbers from last week's baseline, discuss tuning done (continuous batching + queueing), confirm concurrency targets for next overnight run, agree next steps and ownership. Some audio glitches and a couple mis-transcribed words.

Topics:
- Baseline results (hosted vs dedicated)
- Continuous batching behavior and batch size distribution
- Concurrency targets and queueing thresholds
- KV-cache warmup and prefix caching
- Next run plan and observability metrics to capture

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to go over the throughput numbers and next run. Maya, Lucas, can you hear us ok?
[00:08] Maya: yeah we hear you, all good. thanks.
[00:12] Devon: quick note, audio was a tad choppy on my side earlier, apologies if I drop a word.
[00:18] Lucas: nah it's fine, go ahead.
[00:20] Avery: cool. recap from last week - we ran the mixed workload on hosted cluster and then on a dedicated test pool. Hosted got to roughly 320 rps sustained with median latency around 270ms, dedicated with tuned batching hit 610 rps but with 3x less token cost approx.
[00:38] Priya: right, the cost delta was big which is promising, our concern is the tail latencies when we push concurrency.
[00:45] Devon: mm-hmm. the tail's driven by small batches turning into many tiny kernel launches. continuous batching setting we pushed reduces that by grouping small requests for up to 40ms or until batch size 48. we saw average batch size go from 6 to 22.
[01:05] Maya: i think in the logs we saw a lot of variability though, like sometimes batch sizes spiked to 80 when traffic came in bursts. is that expected?
[01:12] Devon: yeah it's expected with bursty traffic, but it actually helps throughput. the tricky part is queueing - if you let the queue grow beyond threshold it increases p99. we recommended a soft queue cap of 120ms wait or max queued requests 200 per worker.
[01:28] Lucas: question - for the dedicated pool, what concurrency per GPU should we aim for? we have A10s in staging, will move to A100s for prod.
[01:35] Avery: from our experiments, target concurrency per GPU depends on model and seq len. For your 1.3B conversational model at median seq 120toks we're recommending 40-60 concurrent on A10 and 120-160 on A100 when combined with continuous batching and prefix cache.
[01:53] Priya: that's a big difference. can we hit 120 on A100 without p99 blowing up?
[01:58] Devon: yes if you apply three configs together: continuous batching (40ms window / max batch 96), KV-cache warmup (preload common prefixes), and a concurrency-based queueing policy that drops to permissive mode under overload. in our staged runs we saw p99 stay under 750ms at 120 concurrency.
[02:18] Maya: the p99 under 750ms \u2014 was that on the same dataset? we have heavier multi-turn across some endpoints.
[02:23] Devon: the run used a sample of your traffic Maya sent last week, scaled to target rps. multi-turn sequences increased avg tokens per request by ~1.6x. so numbers are conservative but still representative.
[02:35] Lucas: can you explain the KV-cache warmup? we saw some cold-start spikes when user sessions first hit the model.
[02:41] Avery: sure, KV-cache warmup is a short preload phase where we pre-populate the attention kv cache for commonly seen prefixes using a small batch job before routing production requests. it reduces first-token latency for multi-turn. Devon has a script prototype.
[02:56] Devon: yeah i pushed the warmup script to the shared drive, it's rough but works. it primes top 50 prefixes, and we saw first-token latency drop by ~220ms in our tests.
[03:08] Maya: nice, can you share that?
[03:10] Devon: will share after this call.
[03:12] Priya: on autoscaling, we need a policy that keeps cost predictable but allows burst. are you suggesting reserved baseline plus burst pool?
[03:20] Avery: yes; reserved for baseline with committed concurrency, then burst capacity for spikes. we can recommend autoscale policy: baseline 60% of expected concurrency, burst up to 200% for short intervals with burst billing.
[03:32] Lucas: any risk with fallbacks? like if dedicated is saturated, do you route to hosted and what about data-exfil concerns?
[03:38] Avery: we support automated fallback to hosted or alternate region, but for Novapay we flagged data residency/security so fallback would be to a compatible private pool only unless you allow hosted for non-sensitive routes. we can gate that per-route.
[03:53] Maya: ok good. about the overnight run \u2014 what metrics should we capture so we can compare?
[03:58] Devon: capture rps, avg/p50/p90/p99 latency for token and request, batch size distribution, queue wait times histogram, GPU utilization, token cost per 1k tokens, and cache hit ratio. also trace IDs for slow reqs.
[04:12] Priya: also capture failure/retry rates and any OOMs.
[04:15] Devon: yes will include.
[04:17] Avery: plan for next run: Lucas to provision a dedicated staging pool (A100 if available) and run a 12h ramp test to simulate peak + off-peak with target concurrency 800 across pool (approx 120 per GPU). this will give us sustained throughput and cost numbers.
[04:32] Lucas: can do, i'll spin up tomorrow.
[04:35] Maya: we'll provide the traffic profile CSV, Maya: will send it today.
[04:38] Avery: perfect. Devon will share batching config and KV warmup script. Avery to send pricing for dedicated reserved + burst estimate.
[04:45] Priya: small nit - in some earlier transcripts the SEs said the batch hold window was 40ms, is that final?
[04:50] Devon: 40ms is our starting point; we sometimes use 25ms for lower-latency endpoints to keep p50 low, but that reduces throughput. you can set per-route.
[04:59] Maya: are there any auto-tuning suggestions? we'd prefer not to manually tweak every route.
[05:03] Devon: we have heuristics: route by median seq len and qps, pick hold window proportional to median inter-arrival quantile; we can provide a recommended mapping. also Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization/packaging but that's later.
[05:17] Priya: competitors question \u2014 has anyone benchmarked against Anthropic or Vertex?
[05:21] Avery: we do internal comparatives; rough numbers vary by model and infra. we can share a redacted benchmark doc but it's noisy. main point is our blending of continuous batching + routing reduces unit cost which is the primary win.
[05:34] Lucas: are there any config pitfalls we should watch for during the overnight run?
[05:38] Devon: yes: avoid max batch sizes that make GPU OOM, monitor batch size distribution; watch for long queue wait times which increase p99; ensure cache eviction is tuned to your session lengths.
[05:49] Maya: question on observability retention \u2014 can we get token-level traces for only a sampled subset? we don't want to retain everything.
[05:55] Avery: yes sampling is supported, plus token redaction. we'll include sampling config in the docs.
[06:00] Priya: great.
[06:02] (brief cross talk about calendar invites)
[06:10] Avery: ok quick recap of owners and deadlines: Maya to send traffic sample (today), Lucas to provision pool (tomorrow), Devon to share configs (Fri), Avery to send pricing and schedule deep-dive (by Monday).
[06:22] Maya: noted.
[06:24] Lucas: noted.
[06:26] Devon: i'll also include a short runbook for interpreting batch histograms.
[06:30] Priya: thanks all.
[06:32] Avery: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to the configs and the run schedule.
[06:36] (call ends)
